eyebrow: Two ways to run a script
code:
$ bash check-disk.sh
Checking disk space on web-01...
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda1        40G   12G   28G  30% /
Done.

$ chmod +x check-disk.sh
$ ./check-disk.sh
Checking disk space on web-01...
...
caption: bash file.sh works anywhere; chmod +x then ./file.sh runs it directly

eyebrow: Every command leaves behind a number
code:
$ ./check-disk.sh
$ echo $?
0

$ ls /no-such-directory
ls: cannot access '/no-such-directory': No such file or directory
$ echo $?
2
caption: $? holds the exit status of the last command — 0 means success

code:
#!/bin/bash
# check-disk.sh — ops team, Northbridge Retail

THRESHOLD=80
usage=$(df -h / | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}' | tr -d '%')

if [ "$usage" -ge "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: / is at ${usage}%"
else
  echo "OK: / is at ${usage}%"
fi
caption: Shebang, header comment, then logic — variables and if come next lesson
